findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher never checks the grant shortcut (inverted condition, wrong offset)
findings.body:
The grant shortcut is the last 2 characters of the 6-character prefix, at `substring(4, 6)`. The matcher reads `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, which for `onrtac` is `ta`. It also returns `false` when the value *equals* the expected shortcut, so the condition is inverted.

With the current offset the comparison never matches, so the check is a no-op and the matcher passes any `xxxxxx:<uuid>` ID. If someone fixes only the offset, every correct token will fail.

As a result, `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` do not verify that the right grant type is encoded. A grant that wrongly encodes `na` would go unnoticed. A prefix shorter than 5 characters would also throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of failing the match.

Fix: use `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` and also check the prefix length. The comment about the "4th char" is wrong as well.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant type factories and can block server startup
findings.body:
`getShortcut()` is added to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` with no default implementation. Custom grant types built on this SPI will no longer compile.

The runtime impact is worse. A custom factory compiled against the old SPI will throw `AbstractMethodError` when `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls `gtf.getShortcut()` for every registered grant factory. That exception aborts `postInit` and prevents Keycloak from starting.

A factory that returns `null` causes `ConcurrentHashMap.put(null, ...)` to throw NPE in the same place.

Fix: provide a default method, e.g. one returning `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.UNKNOWN`. Alternatively, have the encoder tolerate missing or null shortcuts by mapping them to unknown instead of failing startup.

findings.title: Javadoc says 'usually 3-letter' shortcut, but the default encoder requires exactly 2 characters
findings.body:
The contract tells implementers the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters". `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` assumes every shortcut is exactly 2 characters: `getTokenContextFromTokenId` rejects any prefix whose length is not 6 and slices fixed 2-character segments.

Nothing validates shortcut length at registration in `postInit`, and `encodeTokenId` does not check it either. A custom grant that follows the Javadoc and returns a 3-letter shortcut will issue access tokens (`onrtabc:...`) that the same provider cannot decode; it throws `IllegalArgumentException`.

Fix: document that the shortcut must be exactly 2 characters, and validate the length in `postInit` and in the refresh paths.

findings.title: Client credentials (and UMA) grants never set the GRANT_TYPE attribute, so their tokens are encoded as 'na'
findings.body:
The grant type is put into the `ClientSessionContext` in only a few places: `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse`, ROPC, PreAuthorizedCode, refresh and standard token exchange.

`ClientCredentialsGrantType` is not modified. It builds its response directly with `tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken()` rather than through `createTokenResponse`, so `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` is never set. Every client-credentials access token is therefore encoded with grant shortcut `na`, even though the `cc` shortcut is defined here and the unit test uses `trltcc` as an example.

The UMA permission grant (`pg`) and legacy/V1 token exchange flows have the same problem.

Future consumers (#37117, introspection optimizations) will get wrong context for these tokens. The broken `isAccessTokenId` matcher, and the fact that `expectClientLogin` does not assert `TOKEN_ID`, mean no test catches this.

Fix: set `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())` in `ClientCredentialsGrantType`, and likewise for the other flows that bypass `createTokenResponse`.

findings.title: Copy-paste error: rawTokenId null-check validates grantType instead
findings.body:
`Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` checks `grantType` a second time. `rawTokenId` is never validated, so a null raw ID is accepted silently, and `encodeTokenId` then produces an ID like `onrtac:null`.

Fix: it should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes only because of an NPE from the null sessionFactory
findings.body:
The test factory never calls `postInit`, so `sessionFactory` is null. Decoding `ofrtac:5678` misses `ac` in `grantsByShortcuts`, and `getGrantTypeByShortcut` then calls `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)`, which throws `NullPointerException`.

The test catches any `RuntimeException`, so it passes without ever reaching the intended `IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value 'ac' for grant type")` branch.

Fix: supply a stub `KeycloakSessionFactory` that returns no factories, and assert specifically on `IllegalArgumentException`.

findings.title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed; grantType captured once and not refreshed by setFormParams
findings.body:
The public `Context(Context)` copy constructor is deleted from this public SPI class without any mention in the description. Extensions that wrap or clone a grant context will no longer compile.

Separately, `grantType` is read from `formParams` only in the constructor. `setFormParams(...)` replaces the form parameters but leaves `grantType` stale, so `getGrantType()` can disagree with `getFormParams()`.

Fix: either keep the copy constructor (copying `grantType`), or document the removal. Also either derive `grantType` lazily or update it in `setFormParams`.

findings.title: Access token `jti` format change is user-visible but undocumented
findings.body:
The access token `jti`, and the `token_id` detail on events such as `CODE_TO_TOKEN` and `REFRESH_TOKEN`, change from a plain UUID to `xxxxxx:<uuid>`, which is 43 characters and contains a colon.

Resource servers, event listeners and audit pipelines that validate or store `jti` as a UUID, or in a 36-character column, will break after upgrade.

The PR adds no upgrade or release note for this observable contract change. One should be added.
